BLOCKING_oob_read_segfault.trigger: construct StageAOwner via __new__ + __init__ with an exact-subclass of list whose __len__ over-reports the true element count
BLOCKING_oob_read_segfault.mechanism: StageAOwner_init line 236 accepts list/tuple subclasses (PyList_Check/PyTuple_Check, not CheckExact); line 241 takes n from PySequence_Size(relations), which invokes the attacker-overridable __len__; line 259 PySequence_Fast builds a sequence of the TRUE length; lines 263-265 loop i in [0,n) and call PySequence_Fast_GET_ITEM(fast, i), reading past the real end of the sequence
BLOCKING_oob_read_segfault.consequence: out-of-bounds PyObject* read; the value is handed to admit_one -> PyObject_GetAttrString on a NULL/garbage pointer; deterministic segfault in the CPython 3.11.3 governed interpreter
BLOCKING_oob_read_segfault.asan_report: AddressSanitizer: SEGV on unknown address 0x000000000008 (READ); #0 PyObject_GetAttrString+0xe; #1 StageAOwner_init _p07_native_owner_stage_a.c:265; rdi=0x0 (NULL item pointer)
BLOCKING_oob_read_segfault.author_coverage_gap: the Stage A court's hostile-__len__ test (test_admission_requires_exact_sequence, line 150) uses a NON-list duck-typed class, which PyList_Check rejects before PySequence_Size is ever reached; no test exercises a list/tuple SUBCLASS, so the defect is uncovered
BLOCKING_oob_read_segfault.factory_partial_mitigation: module factory build_stage_a_owner uses Py_TYPE(relations) == &PyList_Type (exact, line 638) and refuses subclasses; the defect is reachable only through the class's own __init__, which is ordinary public Python (StageAOwner.__new__ then .__init__)
BLOCKING_oob_read_segfault.secondary_effect: with __len__ under-reporting, admission silently truncates the relations batch (observed n_relations=1 for a 3-element subclass), also a custody-integrity hazard

custody_diagnostic_refcount_leak.mechanism: StageAOwner_custody_diagnostic builds `rows` (PyList_New), embeds it in the result via Py_BuildValue 's:O' (which INCREFs rows), then returns without Py_DECREF(rows) -> one leaked reference per call
custody_diagnostic_refcount_leak.measurement: 20000 calls -> 20000 additional GC-tracked list objects survive gc.collect() (tracked lists 164 -> 20164)

partial_failure_reinit_refcount_leak.mechanism: StageAOwner_init INCREFs trusted_semantic_hash (line 247-248) before validation completes; if admission later fails the object stays unsealed, so __init__ can be called again and overwrites self->trusted_semhash and self->rels without DECREF/free
partial_failure_reinit_refcount_leak.measurement: 2000 repeated failing __init__ calls -> sys.getrefcount(trusted_semantic_hash) grows by exactly 2000; the previously allocated rels array is also leaked per iteration

no_gc_tracking.detail: the type is not Py_TPFLAGS_HAVE_GC and defines neither tp_traverse nor tp_clear while holding strong references to Python objects (admitted relation, trusted_semantic_hash). A cycle through an admitted relation back to the owner cannot be collected. Not demonstrated to matter for the frozen accepted relation, but it is a real omission for arbitrary admitted objects.

dead_reentrancy_check.detail: StageAOwner_init line 221 `if (Py_TYPE(self) == NULL)` can never be true for a live object; the comment claims reentrancy rejection that this check does not implement. Reentrancy is refused incidentally because a StageAOwner presented as a relation fails the ref/content_hash attribute read.
